
VALIDATE-SPEC-ALIGNMENT
Validate alignment between feature specifications, tests, and implementation

WHEN TO USE
  Use in the validating phase to ensure specifications, tests, and implementation are aligned. This command checks that scenarios have corresponding tests and implementation, helping maintain ACDD discipline.

PREREQUISITES
  • Feature files must exist in spec/features/
  • Work units should be tagged in scenarios with @WORK-UNIT-ID

USAGE
  fspec validate-spec-alignment [feature-files...] [options]

ARGUMENTS
  [feature-files] (optional)
    Feature files to validate (default: all in spec/features). Can be file paths or feature names.

OPTIONS
  --fix
    Automatically fix alignment issues (e.g., create missing coverage mappings)

COMMON PATTERNS
  • Validate before moving to done
    Example: # Check alignment before marking work unit done
fspec validate-spec-alignment

# If issues found, fix them
fspec link-coverage user-auth --scenario "Valid login" --test-file src/__tests__/auth.test.ts --test-lines 10-25

# Re-validate
fspec validate-spec-alignment

# Move to done
fspec update-work-unit-status AUTH-001 done
    undefined

  • Auto-fix alignment issues
    Example: # Run with --fix to automatically resolve issues
fspec validate-spec-alignment --fix

# Review changes
fspec show-coverage user-auth
    undefined

  • Validate specific epic
    Example: # Validate all features in an epic
fspec list-features --epic AUTH | xargs fspec validate-spec-alignment
    undefined


TYPICAL WORKFLOW
  1. Complete implementation → 2. Link coverage: fspec link-coverage <feature> → 3. Validate alignment: fspec validate-spec-alignment → 4. Fix any issues → 5. Move to done: fspec update-work-unit-status <id> done

EXAMPLES
  1. Validate alignment for all feature files
  $ fspec validate-spec-alignment
  ✓ All specs are aligned with tests and implementation

Alignment summary:
  Features checked: 12
  Scenarios checked: 45
  Scenarios with tests: 45
  Test coverage: 100%

  2. Validate specific feature file
  $ fspec validate-spec-alignment spec/features/auth/login.feature
  ✓ All specs are aligned with tests and implementation

  3. Validate and auto-fix alignment issues
  $ fspec validate-spec-alignment spec/features/auth/*.feature --fix
  ✓ Fixed 2 alignment issues
✓ All specs are aligned with tests and implementation

  4. Example with alignment issues found
  $ fspec validate-spec-alignment
  ✗ Found 3 alignment issues
  - Scenario "Valid user login" has no test mapping
  - Scenario "Invalid credentials" test has no implementation
  - Feature file "checkout.feature" has no @WORK-UNIT-ID tags

COMMON ERRORS
  ✗ Found 3 alignment issues
    Fix: Review listed issues and either:
1. Add test mappings: fspec link-coverage <feature> --scenario "<name>" --test-file <file> --test-lines <range>
2. Add implementation: fspec link-coverage <feature> --scenario "<name>" --test-file <file> --impl-file <file> --impl-lines <lines>
3. Tag scenarios: fspec add-tag-to-scenario <feature> "<scenario>" @WORK-UNIT-ID

  ✗ Feature file not found: spec/features/nonexistent.feature
    Fix: Check feature file path or use: fspec list-features

RELATED COMMANDS
  fspec validate
  fspec link-coverage
  fspec show-coverage
  fspec audit-coverage
  fspec update-work-unit-status

NOTES
  • Checks that feature scenarios have corresponding test mappings
  • Verifies that tests have implementation mappings
  • Ensures scenarios are tagged with work unit IDs for traceability
  • --fix option attempts to automatically resolve common issues
  • Exit code 1 if alignment issues found (suitable for CI/CD)
  • Part of ACDD workflow - run before moving to done state
